mapName: A Learnable Russia - No Car Metas - 2

metas.name: Altai landscape
metas.note: The main road of Altai Republic has a black car long antenna driving north through the Altai Mountains, often with foggy or rainy coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Bilingual town names
metas.note: Some republics of Russia with minority languages use bilingual town entry and directional signs, such as in Bashkortostan and Tatarstan displaying Bashkir and Tatar respectively.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Black traffic sign bottom
metas.note: This black traffic sign bottom is primarily found in Stavropol and Chechnya, as well as western Dagestan. Rarely, exceptions can be found in other southern federal subjects such as Kabardino Balkaria, but these will typically be uncolored.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Blue-pod lupines
metas.note: Blue-pod lupines appear very commonly in northern Vladimir Oblast, eastern Ivanovo Oblast, and southwestern Kostroma Oblast. It can also be found less commonly elsewhere in Kirov Oblast and towards the Baltics.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Buryatia haze
metas.note: This forest fire haze is found near Lake Gusinoye, southwest of Ulan-Ude in Buryatia. While similar to the haze found near Mirny, the Buryatia haze coverage can typically be recognised by the open rolling landscape, which is not found near Mirny.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Caucasus mountains
metas.note: The Caucasus mountain range is one of the largest mountain ranges in Russia. The tallest mountain in Russia, Mount Elbrus, can be found on the border of the Kabardino-Balkarian Republic and Karachay-Cherkessia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Clips on signposts
metas.note: Clips on edges of signposts are found in Leningrad and St. Petersburg, and very rarely in Pskov, Novgorod or elsewhere.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Cyrillic and latin town names
metas.note: Town names written in both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabets are common near the Baltic border and around Moscow, and to a lesser extent in federal subjects on the Finnish border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Dagestan landscape
metas.note: Grassy fields, with bushy vegetation, in early spring Generation 4 coverage is typical for Dagestan. The landscape can either be completely flat or mountainous. These flowers are also quite common in the Generation 4 Dagestan coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Kolyma Highway
metas.note: The eastern half of the Kolyma Highway going to Magadan features a lot of tall hills and mountains, usually shrouded in a haze. Most of the roads are unpaved and feature dark gravelly soil. The haze is not present in the western half.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Mosques
metas.note: While mosques can be found everywhere in Russia, they are by far most common in areas with a Muslim majority, mainly in much of south Russia as well as Tatarstan and Bashkortostan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Murmansk landscape
metas.note: An open, hilly landscape with low shrubbery and fireweed usually indicates Murmansk. The lower the shrubbery, the more north it generally is.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Northern Sakhalin
metas.note: The road to Okha in northern Sakhalin is unpaved, revealing its very sandy soil. The road is surrounded by short, stunted bushes and trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Olkhon Island
metas.note: Olkhon Island on Lake Baikal has a single road, driving on rolling sandy hills during sunset. You can often see Lake Baikal directly with a mountain ridge across the bay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Outer dashed road lines
metas.note: Outer dashed road lines are usually found throughout Kursk Oblast. An exception can be found in Tuva Republic. Rarer exceptions include the Republic of Karelia, Primorsky Krai and Khabarovsk Krai.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Sunflowers
metas.note: Sunflowers are common along the border with Ukraine as well as more eastern oblasts like Ulyanovsk, Samara, and northern Orenburg.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Tuva landscape
metas.note: Dry steppe mountains with a long antenna will usually indicate the Tuva Republic. The south part of the main road in the Altai Republic and Tuva can appear similarly dry, so things such as driving direction and cloudiness can be used to distinguish them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Very hazy coverage
metas.note: Very hazy coverage is found east and south of Mirny, especially along the Vilyuy river. The colour of the haze varies, but it is often orange or white.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Vladivostok area
metas.note: Lush and diverse forests in a hilly landscape characterises the noticeably warmer region around Vladivostok. Most of the coverage is overcast and has a white car with a long antenna. Further south, near the tri-border, you will find a more open rolling hill landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: White flower
metas.note: This type of white flower (heracleum sosnowskyi) is most commonly found around Moscow, Komi Republic, and Perm Krai.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.
